record.context_brief: Non-ample fields satisfying the Debes-Deschamps conjecture
record.original_question: Does there exist a non-ample field K such that every finite split embedding problem over K has a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field K for which the Debes-Deschamps conjecture holds?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1 (D`ebes-Deschamps). Every finite split embedding problem over any field K has a regular solution.
Question VI. Does there exist a non-ample field K for which the conjecture of D`ebes and Deschamps holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K be a field. A finite embedding problem over K is a pair (φ: Gal(K) ↠ G, α: H ↠ G), where Gal(K) is the absolute Galois group of K, H and G are finite groups, φ is a continuous surjection, and α is a surjection of finite groups. The embedding problem is called split if α admits a group-theoretic section G → H. A regular solution to the embedding problem is a Galois extension F of the rational function field K(t) such that:
(i) F/K(t) is regular (i.e., K is algebraically closed in F),
(ii) Gal(F/K(t)) ≅ H, and
(iii) the natural restriction Gal(F/K(t)) → Gal(K) factors through φ via α (i.e., F yields a proper solution of the embedding problem over K(t)).

The Debes–Deschamps conjecture asserts: for every field K, every finite split embedding problem over K admits a regular solution.

A field K is called ample (or large) if every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points; equivalently, K is existentially closed in the Laurent series field K((t)). The conjecture is known to hold for all ample fields.

Question: Does there exist a non-ample field K such that every finite split embedding problem over K has a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field K for which the Debes–Deschamps conjecture holds?
artifact.category_tag: Inverse Galois theory and embedding problems
artifact.status_search_result: The Debes–Deschamps conjecture is established for ample (large) fields via results of Pop, Haran–Jarden, and others. Whether any non-ample field satisfies the conjecture appears to remain open: web searches surface surveys of split embedding problems over ample fields and complete domains, but no result establishing the conjecture for a non-ample field was found.

status_evidence.title: Split embedding problems over complete domains
status_evidence.snippet: Every finite split embedding problem over a field that is the quotient field of a suitable complete domain is regularly solvable.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is verified in ample/complete-domain settings, leaving non-ample case open.

status_evidence.title: The Regular Inverse Galois Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the regular inverse Galois and split embedding problems, with status over ample fields.
status_evidence.claim: Known progress concentrates on ample fields; non-ample case not reported as resolved.
